steps.label: Count how many subsets there must be
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the count before the list. It is the check that the list is complete.
lines: The power set P(A) is the set of all subsets of A.
n(P(A)) = 2³ = 8, so eight subsets must be listed.

recall.must_convey: That P(A) is the set of all subsets of A and that there are 2³ = 8 of them.
accept: the power set is the set of all subsets so there are two cubed which is eight
n of A is three so eight subsets
two to the power three gives eight subsets
power set ante anni subsets, moodu elements kabatti enimidi
count the subsets first, two power n

steps.why: Knowing the answer must hold eight members turns the listing into a check. A list of seven or nine is then noticed on the page instead of after the paper is handed in.
common_mistakes: Saying there are 6 subsets after counting only the non-empty ones with fewer than three members.
steps.memory_tip: Each element is either taken or left out, so three elements give 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 subsets.

steps.label: List all eight subsets
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Members of P(A) are sets, so each one is written inside its own braces.

recall.must_convey: That the eight subsets are listed, including the empty set and A itself.
accept: empty set, the three single element sets, the three pairs and A itself
list them by size none one two and three
phi then minus three then zero then three then the pairs then the whole set
empty set nunchi start chesi, singles, pairs, chivarlo whole set
all eight subsets including the null set and A

steps.why: Listing by size covers every subset exactly once, and the group sizes 1, 3, 3, 1 add to the 8 counted in the first step.
common_mistakes: Leaving out ∅, which is a subset of every set.
Leaving out A itself, which is also a subset of A.
Writing the members −3, 0, 3 instead of the one-element sets {−3}, {0}, {3}.
steps.memory_tip: List by size — none, one, two, three — and the group counts read 1, 3, 3, 1.
